_comment: Out-of-sample baseline-level backtests for STATE tax-credit programs: the populace baseline weighted total of each state credit variable (defined_for its state, so the national sum IS the state total) vs an official state statistic, or a documented approximation where none exists (benchmark.score_type='approximation'). None of these totals are calibration targets. Dataset period is 2024; benchmark.year records the statistic's tax/fiscal year, so one-year vintage gaps apply as with the SOI levels. Excluded, with reasons: VA (va_eitc pays the better of a refundable and a nonrefundable credit, so no single published line matches the variable); GA/DC/RI CTCs and the PA EITC (not in effect in 2024); CT CTC (no ongoing credit, only a one-time 2022 rebate); ME Dependent Exemption Tax Credit (Maine publishes only the refundable excess over liability); UT CTC (no official statistic; heavily liability-limited).

levels.name: California CalEITC

benchmark.source: CA FTB, California EITC / YCTC / FYTC Report (Oct 2025), Table 1 p.8

levels.description: Refundable; 3,340,639 returns, avg $282. Tax-year basis (process-year basis is $986M). TY2024 report not yet published, so a one-year vintage gap applies.

levels.name: California Young Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: CA FTB, California EITC / YCTC / FYTC Report (Oct 2025), Table 1 p.8

levels.description: Refundable; 398,059 returns, 483,629 qualifying children. Gap analysis (2026-07 audit): +38.7% vs TY2023 = ~6pp benchmark vintage (max $1,117 -> $1,154, phase-out start $25,775 -> $26,626: +6.2% measured on the same data) + ~30pp take-up. The model pays every eligible unit: 546-559k eligible units in the data vs FTB's 398,059 actual returns (claim/eligible 0.71-0.73, matching published take-up: CalEITC 54% among SNAP-enrolled per CPL/JPubE 2023). Per-unit amounts align ($1,025 sim vs $1,037 actual) — the gap is purely excess unit count; demographics ruled out (weighted CA under-6 is 6.2% BELOW ACS 2024). A flat per-return credit passes the take-up gap straight to the total.

levels.name: New York EITC

benchmark.source: NYS DTF open data, EITC Claims by Place of Residence, Table 3 (Grand Total)

levels.description: Refundable, 30% of federal less the household credit; 1,435,448 claims. NYS EITC only - the separate NYC and noncustodial EITCs are excluded from both sides.

levels.name: New York Empire State Child Credit

benchmark.source: NYS DTF open data, Empire State Child Credit Study by Place of Residence

levels.description: Refundable; 1,451,132 claims, 2,429,901 qualifying children. TY2023 and the 2024 dataset period both use the regular 33%-of-federal structure with the under-4 expansion; the age-based restructure begins 2025. Excludes the one-time 2024 supplemental checks.

levels.name: Colorado EITC

benchmark.source: CO DOR Office of Research and Analysis, Individual Income Tax Credits TY2023 (updated Mar 2026)

levels.description: Refundable; 311,343 claims, avg $1,145. TY2023 used a one-year 50% match and the 2024 model year is also 50% (HB24-1134), so the rates align. A further $23.1M Expanded COEITC (ITIN and under-25 filers) is reported separately; populace models the under-25 expansion, so its total may sit between the two figures.

levels.name: Colorado Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: CO DOR Office of Research and Analysis, Individual Income Tax Credits TY2023 (updated Mar 2026)

levels.description: Refundable; 130,188 claims, avg $685. Children under 6, 10-60% of the federal CTC by AGI tier. Vintage caveat (2026-07 audit): the +30.4% gap is entirely law-change vintage, proven by replication — running the pre-HB23-1112 TY2023 law (60/30/10% of federal CTC) on this same data reproduces the DOR actual to the dollar ($89.2M vs $89,158,930), and the TY2024 flat-amount restructure (HB23-1112: $1,200/$600/$200 per under-6 child-dependent, $0-earners newly eligible) adds +30.0%. Against the bill's own fiscal-note-implied TY2024 level (~$135M) the sim runs ~14% under. Replace with CO DOR TY2024 actuals when published.

levels.name: Washington Working Families Tax Credit

benchmark.source: WA DOR, WFTC Program 2025 Report to the Legislature (Dec 2025), Tables 2 and 4

levels.description: 284,416 approved applications as of Oct 2025. Claims may be filed up to three years late, so the published total still grows; populace, which assumes take-up among modeled eligibles, should sit at or above it.

levels.name: Minnesota Child Tax Credit + Working Family Credit

benchmark.source: MN House Research, Minnesota Child Credit and Working Family Credit (May 2026), p.1

levels.description: The two credits share one phase-out and populace computes them as one combined variable. House Research combined cost: 240,100 returns with children (avg $2,773) plus 301,500 childless returns (avg $297). MN DOR separately reports the CTC share as $564M across 219k families and 447k children.

levels.name: Minnesota Working Family Credit

benchmark.source: Derived: House Research combined CTC+WFC $755.5M minus MN DOR CTC $564M (both TY2024)

levels.description: No standalone official WFC total is published; this subtracts two official figures from different sources, so treat as approximate. The childless-return subtotal ($89.6M) is a clean official lower bound.

levels.name: Connecticut EITC

benchmark.source: CT DRS Annual Report FY2024-25, p.35

levels.description: Fully refundable, 40% of federal; 193,283 credits. The $250-per-filer qualifying-child supplement begins TY2025 and is excluded from both sides.

levels.name: New Mexico Working Families Tax Credit

benchmark.source: 2025 New Mexico Tax Expenditure Report (TRD), p.259 (reliability 1: separately reported actuals)

levels.description: Refundable, 25% of federal; 201,819 claims.

levels.name: New Mexico Child Income Tax Credit

benchmark.source: 2025 New Mexico Tax Expenditure Report (TRD), p.81 (reliability 1)

levels.description: Refundable, $25-$600 per child stepping down with AGI; 243,909 claiming returns.

levels.name: Rhode Island EITC

benchmark.source: 2026 RI Tax Expenditures Report (Office of Revenue Analysis, Jan 2026), Credits item 8, p.77

levels.description: Refundable; 73,463 taxpayers. TY2023 used the 15% match; the 2024 model year is 16%, so populace should run roughly 7% above (ORA projects TY2024 at $29.8M).

levels.name: Illinois EITC

benchmark.source: IDOR, Individual Income Tax Returns by AGI, TY2023 final stratification (Nov 2025), p.1

levels.description: Refundable, 20% of federal in both TY2023 and the 2024 model year; 899,078 Illinois-resident returns. The all-filer total including non-IL addresses is $451.0M; populace models residents.

levels.name: Hawaii EITC

benchmark.source: HI DOTAX, Earned Income Tax Credit Report TY2024 (Act 107 report, Dec 2025), Table 1 p.5

levels.description: Refundable, 40% of federal; 78,399 new-credit claims. Excludes pre-2023 nonrefundable-credit carryover the report also counts.

levels.name: Iowa EITC

benchmark.source: IA DOR, Tax Credits Contingent Liabilities Report (Mar 2026), Tables 2 and 8

levels.description: Refundable, 15% of federal. FY2025 actual claims basis.

levels.name: Kansas EITC

benchmark.source: KS DOR, Tax Expenditure Report CY2024, Earned Income Credit (K.S.A. 79-32,205), p.9

levels.description: Refundable, 17% of federal; 171,232 claims (process year 2024, i.e. TY2023 returns).

levels.name: Louisiana EITC

benchmark.source: LA DOR, Tax Exemption Budget 2025-2026, item 78, p.38

levels.description: Refundable, 5% of federal. Fiscal-year revenue-loss basis (FYE June 2025, mostly TY2024 returns).

levels.name: Nebraska EITC

benchmark.source: NE DOR, Nebraska Statistics of Individual Income Tax, Table F2 2024 (refundable credits)

levels.description: Refundable, 10% of federal; 111,150 claims. Residents only.

levels.name: Wisconsin Earned Income Credit

benchmark.source: WI Legislative Fiscal Bureau, Updated Tax Information for 2025 LFB Informational Papers (Apr 2025), Tables 8-10

levels.description: Refundable, 4/11/34% of federal by number of children (childless ineligible); 193,799 claims, avg $453.

levels.name: Vermont EITC

benchmark.source: 2025 Vermont Tax Expenditures Biennial Report (JFO and Dept of Taxes, Jan 2025), Appendix C p.77

levels.description: Refundable, 38% of federal in both TY2022 and the 2024 model year (the childless rate rises to 100% only from TY2025); 33,520 returns. Oldest benchmark in this file - a two-year vintage gap applies.

levels.name: Vermont Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: 2025 Vermont Tax Expenditures Biennial Report, Appendix C p.77; VT JFO one-year lookback brief (Dec 2023)

levels.description: Refundable, $1,000 per child under 6 with a 2% per $1,000 phase-out above $125k AGI; 21,296 returns, 27,214 children. Age limit rises to under 7 only from TY2025.

levels.name: Maryland EITC (refundable + nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: Comptroller of Maryland, Income Tax Summary Report TY2024, refund summary pp.18-19 and selected credits pp.21-23

levels.description: Sum of two official lines: $410.1M refunded EIC (361,865 returns) plus $140.8M nonrefundable EIC claimed against liability (246,823 returns) - populace md_eitc pays whichever of the two credits is larger per filer, matching the summed concept. The local EITC is netted out of local tax and never published.

levels.name: Oregon EITC

benchmark.source: TY2023 Oregon Personal Income Tax Statistics (150-101-406, revised), Exhibits 36 and 38

levels.description: Refundable, 9% of federal (12% with a child under 3); 212,930 full-year-resident returns including ITIN filers. Full-year residents only - all-filer totals run 6-7% higher, so populace should land at or slightly above.

levels.name: Oregon Kids Credit

benchmark.source: TY2023 Oregon Personal Income Tax Statistics (150-101-406, revised), Exhibit 36

levels.description: Refundable, $1,000 per child 0-5 with a $25k-$30k MAGI phase-out; 30,110 full-year-resident returns, avg $1,140. DOR reported over $39M across all filers; official take-up is roughly half of eligible families, while populace assumes full take-up - expect populace above the benchmark.

levels.name: Maryland Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: Maryland Tax Expenditures Report FY2024 (DBM Bureau of Revenue Estimates), pp.23 and 47

levels.description: Refundable $500 per child under 6 (or disabled under 17) for AGI under $15k. FY2024 reflects TY2023, the first expanded year; the report's EITC lines match tax-year actuals exactly, so the figure is claims-based. No claim counts published.

levels.name: New Jersey EITC

benchmark.source: NJ Tax Expenditure Report FY2027 (Treasury/Taxation), item 40 p.33: 617,800 claims x $977 average

levels.description: Refundable, 40% of federal. Total computed from printed claims and average (total not printed), so treat as approximate; the report projects $628.1M for FY2027.

levels.name: New Jersey Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: NJ Tax Expenditure Report FY2027 (Treasury/Taxation), item 63 p.44: 232,500 credits x $949 average

levels.description: Refundable, $200-$1,000 per child under 6 by income tier up to $80k. Total computed from printed claims and average.

levels.name: Massachusetts EITC

benchmark.source: MA FY26 Tax Expenditure Budget, item 1.605

levels.description: Refundable, 40% of federal from TY2023. Fiscal-year tax-expenditure estimate (no claim counts published); FY2025 estimate is $341.4M.

levels.name: Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit

benchmark.source: MA FY26 Tax Expenditure Budget, item 1.628

levels.description: Refundable, uncapped $440 per dependent from TY2024. The FY2025 estimate reflects the $440 rate that also applies in the 2024 model year (FY2024 reflected the first-year $310 rate).

levels.name: Maine EITC

benchmark.source: Maine State Tax Expenditure Report 2026-2027 (MRS Office of Tax Policy), item 1.032 p.36

levels.description: Refundable, 25% of federal (50% for childless filers); roughly 92,000 taxpayers. Microsimulation-based fiscal-year revenue-loss estimate, net of a TANF-fund offset.

levels.name: Michigan EITC

benchmark.source: MI Treasury press releases (Oct 2025, Apr 2024): about 665,000 claims at an $890 average

levels.description: Refundable, 30% of federal. Total implied from the printed claim count and average (Treasury prints no total), so treat as approximate.

levels.name: Montana EITC

benchmark.source: Approximation: 10% statutory match x $156.1M federal EITC claimed in MT (IRS EITC Central, TY2024 returns processed in 2025)

levels.description: Montana's match rose from 3% to 10% in TY2024; the only official actual ($3.9M, DOR biennial report Table 3.13) is from the 3% era, so the IRS-derived figure is the fairer current-rate benchmark.

levels.name: Indiana EITC

benchmark.source: 2024 Indiana Tax Expenditure Review (LSA OFMA, Oct 2024), item IT42 p.21

levels.description: Refundable, 10% of federal under Indiana-specific qualifying rules. FY2024 LSA estimate (latest actual is FY2022 at $77.5M, before the 10% recoupling).

levels.name: Oklahoma EITC

benchmark.source: Oklahoma Tax Commission, Tax Expenditure Report 2023-2024, income tax credits item 13, p.6 (reliability level 1)

levels.description: Refundable, 5% of federal computed under frozen pre-2021 federal parameters, so an IRS-derived approximation is invalid here; the official TY2022 actual (321,693 claims) is the best available despite the two-year vintage gap.

levels.name: Delaware EITC

benchmark.source: 2025 Delaware Tax Preference Report, Personal Income Tax chapter section 1.16, p.1-28

levels.description: Filers choose a 20% nonrefundable or 4.5% refundable credit; Delaware publishes only an estimated fiscal-year revenue loss (FY2026 estimate: $18.0-18.5M), with no claim counts.

levels.name: District of Columbia EITC

benchmark.source: DC Tax Expenditure Report (OCFO/ORA, Sept 2024), item 129 p.235

levels.description: Refundable; ORA revenue-loss estimate at the 70% match in force for TY2022-2024 (the match rises to 100% in TY2025). Latest published actual is TY2021 ($69.6M at the 40% match). Credits of $1,200+ are paid in monthly installments, blurring fiscal-year timing.

levels.name: Illinois Child Tax Credit

benchmark.source: Illinois State Budget FY2027 (GOMB, Feb 2026), p.28

levels.description: Refundable, 20% of the filer's Illinois EITC (child under 12) in TY2024, doubling to 40% for TY2025+. GOMB statewide estimate - no official actuals or claim counts published yet.

levels.name: Arizona Dependent Tax Credit

benchmark.source: Approximation: ACS 2024 1-year age counts for Arizona x statutory amounts ($100 per dependent under 17, $25 at 17+)

levels.description: About 1.49M Arizonans under 17 x $100 plus roughly 99k 17-year-olds x $25. Upper bound: the credit phases out above $200k single / $400k joint AGI, and 18+ dependents (omitted here) partially offset that.

levels.name: Idaho Grocery Credit

benchmark.source: Approximation: ACS 2024 1-year Idaho population (2,001,619) x the $120 per-person credit

levels.description: Upper bound: the credit is prorated by months not receiving SNAP and excludes incarcerated months, and the seniors add-on ($20, in force through 2024) is omitted; expect populace below the benchmark. Note: the 2,001,619 population figure matches the Census Vintage-2024 PEP estimate rather than the cited ACS 1-year table; either way an upper-bound approximation.

levels.name: Virginia EITC / low-income credit (Sec. 58.1-339.8, all elections)

benchmark.source: VA TAX Annual Report FY2025, Table 3.1 ($224,156,631, 522,435 returns); RD717 FY2025 Tax Preferences Report Table 2 p.7 splits the 15% refundable election at $130.39M/253,759 returns

levels.description: Va. Code 58.1-339.8 offers three mutually exclusive elections: $300/exemption low-income credit (CLI), 20% nonrefundable EITC, or 15% refundable EITC (20% refundable starts TY2025). policyengine-us embeds the election inside va_eitc (the nonrefundable branch takes max(20% x federal EITC, CLI) via va_non_refundable_eitc_if_claimed), so va_eitc alone is the whole-section comparator — do NOT add va_low_income_tax_credit on top (it is an intermediate; summing double-counts, verified: sum $511M vs official $224M). FY-processed basis mixes tax years (FY2024 comparator: $207.5M).

levels.name: Ohio EITC (30% nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: OH Tax Expenditure Report FY2026-27, item 2.23 (GRF revenue foregone; FY2024 $56.4M, FY2025 $59.3M, FY2026 $60.9M — all estimates from ODT return data)

levels.description: R.C. 5747.71, 30% of federal EITC, nonrefundable against liability after most other credits. FY2025 captures TY2024 filings. Ohio exempts income below ~$26k, so the low-income liability available to offset is thin — the model's capping fidelity drives this row.

levels.name: Missouri Working Family Tax Credit (20% nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: MO DOR Working Family Tax Credits Issued Calendar Year 2025: $46,062,034, 182,367 credits, avg $252.58 (Sec. 143.177.5 reports prior tax year; 20% rate confirmed for TY2024, trigger fired). TY2023 at 10%: $28.5M

levels.description: Sec. 143.177, 20% of federal EITC from TY2024, nonrefundable with no carryforward (issued = used).

levels.name: South Carolina EITC (125% nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: SC RFA Tax Expenditure Report (Jan 27 2026), p.6: $23.22M FY2024-25 estimated GF revenue loss. Concept note: SC DOR reports $212.0M CLAIMED on TY2023 returns (99,122 credits) — a ~9x claimed-vs-used wedge from nonrefundability plus SC's 0% bracket

levels.description: Sec. 12-6-3632, 125% of federal EITC, nonrefundable, full-year residents. The revenue-loss (used) concept matches the model's liability-limited variable; the claimed amount would be the pre-offset 125% computation.

levels.name: Colorado Family Affordability Credit (refundable)

benchmark.source: HB24-1311 Final Fiscal Note (Aug 5 2024), Table 1: -$327M FY2023-24 (half-year accrual) and 'up to -$684M' FY2024-25; implied full-TY2024 = 2 x $327M = $654M at the note's ~75% take-up (~$880M at 100%). C.R.S. 39-22-130; TY2024 pays full statutory $3,200 (age 0-5) / $2,400 (6-16) — the surplus trigger starts TY2025

levels.description: No CO DOR TY2024 actuals yet (the DOR credits dataset still ends TY2023). populace pays every eligible unit, so the like-for-like comparison is the note's 100%-take-up ~$880M; the headline benchmark is the note's take-up-adjusted central. Flat per-child refundable credit — same take-up exposure class as CA YCTC (populace#341). Replace with DOR actuals when published.

levels.name: Idaho Child Tax Credit ($205/child nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: ID DFM General Fund Revenue Book, Jan 2026 ed. p.20, Idaho Tax Preferences row 63-3029L: $63.962M CY2024 (Jan 2025 ed. had $66.475M); DFM foregone-revenue estimate, no Tax Commission actuals published

levels.description: Sec. 63-3029L, $205 per qualifying child, nonrefundable, residents, sunsets after TY2025.

levels.name: Utah Child Tax Credit ($1,000/child ages 1-3, nonrefundable)

benchmark.source: UT State Tax Commission, Individual Income Tax Credits Claimed by Tax Year 2010-2024 (Apr 30 2026), Nonrefundable Child Tax Credit row: $40,022,410 / 39,754 returns TY2024. Concept: amount CLAIMED (avg ~$1,007 = the per-child amount, i.e. pre-offset); the HB170 fiscal note projected only $9.63M FY2025 revenue impact

levels.description: Utah Code 59-10-1047 (HB170 2023): $1,000 per child aged 1-3 at year-end, nonrefundable, phased out $0.10/$1 above $27k MFS / $43k single-HoH / $54k MFJ. The 4x claimed-vs-fiscal-note wedge and the model's liability/ordering caps both bear on this row — treat large errors as a concept flag first. HB153 adds age 4 only from TY2025.
